title: The Archive of the Kuiper Line Revisited
premise: Juniper Oyelaran, a clone of a murdered beacon-keeper, has spent six years maintaining the Kuiper Line relay and the cold case that came with her predecessor's memories. When a ship that never flew appears on her scopes carrying a passenger name absent from every archive, she discovers the original Juniper was killed because she found proof the fleet's founding truce was built on an erased massacre. Pursued by loyalists who need the record to stay buried and haunted by memories that may have been edited, Juniper races a dying signal toward the deep relay where the truth is stored. At the relay she must choose between broadcasting the massacre and preserving the fragile truce that keeps thousands alive — and she finds a third path: giving the truth only to those who were erased, letting them decide. The fleet survives, changed; Juniper finally becomes someone other than a copy.
about_author: Rosalind Ishikawa is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing maintenance manuals for stations nobody visited, which taught her that loneliness is a plot structure. She writes science fiction about people who inherit other people's problems, literally or otherwise.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She performs her daily maintenance ritual on the Kuiper Line relay, narrating the routines inherited from the original's muscle memory. A routine audit reveals a commissioning order with no author, no date, no funding trail. The emotional beat is quiet unease — the first crack in a life built on repetition.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The freighter Vesperine, decommissioned before Juniper's birth, pings the relay with a valid flight plan. Its manifest lists one passenger: 'Adaeze Oyelaran' — a name from the original's childhood that exists in no database. Juniper logs it officially while privately panicking.

chapters.title: Muscle Memory Lies
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, intercut with recovered log entries from the original. Testing her own memories against physical records, Juniper finds three days of her clone-growth period unaccounted for. The beat is vertigo: if her memory was edited, which Juniper made these repairs?

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The Vesperine docks despite having no crew heat signature. Inside: dust undisturbed for decades, and a single live stasis pod with Adaeze inside — biologically twenty years old, chronologically ninety. The chapter ends as the pod opens.

chapters.title: What the Dead Girl Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Juniper and Adaeze. Adaeze wakes believing the original Juniper is still alive; the confrontation between the copy and the sister who knew the source is brutal and tender. Adaeze reveals she boarded the Vesperine fleeing something, not seeking anything. Beat: grief with teeth.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet-side POV: Warden Ilsa Reyes-Mbeki aboard the flagship Concordance reviews the same anomaly Juniper found, flagged by automated loyalty systems. We learn the fleet's founding truce expires in forty days unless renewed by unanimous council vote — and one vote is already wavering. Beat: institutional dread.

chapters.title: The Erased Massacre
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. She explains why she ran: her family kept a private archive proving the colony Callisto Verde — three thousand people — was destroyed by the fleet itself during the Unification, then written out of history. The original Juniper had found corroborating data in the relay's deep storage. Beat: the case stops being a murder and becomes a cover-up.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Editing
chapters.summary: Reyes-Mbeki's POV. Ordered to retrieve the Vesperine's black box and 'sanitize' the beacon, she hesitates — her own grandmother's name appears in a Callisto Verde casualty fragment she was told was corrupted data. Beat: the antagonist becomes a person.

chapters.title: Signal Decay
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The proof in the relay's deep storage is degrading; the original encoded it in volatile memory to keep it off any network, meaning it dies unless physically carried to the outer relay at the edge of dead space. They have thirty-one days. Beat: the race begins.

chapters.title: Provisions and Precedents
chapters.summary: Juniper and Adaeze prepare the only flight-capable vessel at the beacon — the original's hidden skiff, stocked years ago for exactly this trip, which proves the original planned her own escape and never got to use it. Beat: mourning someone you are.

chapters.title: The Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: Reyes-Mbeki's POV. She launches interception but deliberately files a slow trajectory, buying the fugitives time while telling herself it's procedure. Her second-in-command notices. Beat: complicity begins as a rounding error.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. In the silence beyond the last buoy, with nothing to maintain, Juniper and Adaeze finally talk about what a clone owes the dead. Adaeze admits she resents loving someone who is a reprint. Beat: the relationship breaks open honestly.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Shoal
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Loyalist hardliners, acting without Reyes-Mbeki's authorization, ambush the skiff in a debris shoal. Adaeze takes a hull breach injury shielding the data core. They escape, barely. Beat: the stakes turn physical and irreversible.

chapters.title: The Med Bay Confession
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV, feverish. Under pain meds she confesses she didn't just flee the archive — she stole it, dooming her family to reprisal, and she chose the Vesperine because the original Juniper once promised her sanctuary there. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Reyes Defects
chapters.summary: Reyes-Mbeki's POV. Confronted with her own falsified intercept reports, she goes fully rogue, transmitting the true pursuit timeline to Juniper and turning her ship toward the outer relay herself. Beat: loyalty realigns around truth rather than institution.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They reach the ancient relay — older than the fleet, predating the truce, built by the very colonists the histories erased. Its systems recognize Adaeze's family encryption. Beat: awe, and the sense of being expected.

chapters.title: Broadcast Window
chapters.summary: Triple POV converging. The full archive assembles: the massacre, the cover-up, and — the twist — evidence the truce itself was negotiated over Callisto Verde's silent grave, meaning exposure could shatter the peace. The council vote is in nine hours. Beat: the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Juniper Would Do
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Hardliners board the relay; Reyes-Mbeki holds the docking ring at gunpoint, buying minutes. Juniper must decide alone what the original would have done — and realizes the question is wrong. She isn't the original. Beat: identity resolved into agency.

chapters.title: The Third Path
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. Instead of fleet-wide broadcast, Juniper routes the archive through the old colonists' network — delivering the truth directly to the descendants of the erased, scattered throughout the fleet, and lets them choose whether to speak. The truth spreads person by person, ungovernable. Beat: catharsis through distribution of power.

chapters.title: Truce, Amended
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The council reconvenes facing a fleet that already knows; the truce passes unanimously but amended — Callisto Verde written back into the charter, reparations begun. Hardliners stand down, outflanked by their own constituents. Beat: exhausted, earned hope.

chapters.title: Afterimages
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV. Recovery, and the awkward work of building a relationship with Juniper that isn't a shadow of the dead. Adaeze chooses to stay at the beacon — not as sanctuary, but as home. Beat: grief settling into love.

chapters.title: The Keeper, Signed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She amends the beacon's commissioning record, entering her own name as author — the first entry in the archive that belongs to her alone. The final line mirrors the opening ritual, now chosen rather than inherited. Beat: quiet, complete resolution.
